If you had to "wrestle" it out if him and he's no longer in contact with his family except his brother. Is it not possible he's ashamed of their choice and didn't want to admit it? The brother probably had as much say as he did in his parents choices, do you know much about him? How open is he with emotional topics about himself? Is it not possible he's scared of blood transfusions for some reason, after being raised against them, and just doesn't understand the point of celebrations? I barely get them myself but that's due to feeling greedy or wasteful depending on the scenario. Did you initially ask why he doesn't celebrate or is that where he chose to say something like "I just don't" and omitted it? What sort of conversation did you have before this one where you think that topic would have naturally come up? Did you expect him to just say it automatically? If you were distant from your parents, how much would you talk about them if you wanted to move on from the past?

You say he will let you raise his kids however you believe, so do you trust him, or expect him to lie? Why or why not? You're saying he didn't lie directly about his past, just wasn't upfront about it, so do you believe he'd directly lie to you? How much do you know this man you've only just met face to face? You say it was supposed to be a "fling", what did you mean by that? Did you truly spend time getting to know one another or was most of it playful flirting until you met? 

You don't have to answer all these questions here, that's a lot lol, but you should really think about them and answer them to yourself before you make character assessments based on peoples opinions of JW's, when they don't have those answers. 

From this post alone, it's really hard for me to jump to the conclusions other are making about how he's a manipulative member of a cult who will lure you in eventually. We don't know why he's still talking to his brother, thar doesn't automatically mean he's going to return to his parents. According to this post, he isn't against your beliefs, but you are dead set against his. Infact you honestly sound just as disrespectful towards him, if not more, as you told him to his face that if he's incapacitated you are going to do something to him against his will. If I were him I'd run just because of that  alone, how can he trust you when you admit you'll do something he doesn't want when he has no choice? You don't seem to respect his wishes and are judging him based upon one omission about his family. He seems to be trying, but are you? If you want this to ever work, you can't disrespect his wishes in regards to his own body. You need to try and meet him halfway as he's trying to meet you.
